stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
Key technologies involved include transformers and safetensors, central to modern NLP.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Google will now let any AI agent run your smart home
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Google is enabling third-party AI agents (like Claude) to interact with smart home ecosystems.
This functionality is powered by a new standardized integration called the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
The change allows external AI tools to control devices and analyze home data, marking a significant shift in smart home interoperability.

stories.title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: The Ars Technica review
stories.author: Andrew Cunningham
bullet_points: The review covers macOS 27, codenamed Golden Gate.
The update is characterized as both a minor iteration ('Snow Leopard update') and a major advancement.
A key focus of the update is the integration and impact of Apple Intelligence.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes modern ML components such as transformers and safetensors, indicating relevance in the LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when tested against the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Apple might make servers again to cash in on the AI rush
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly planning a return to the server hardware market.
The move is driven by the escalating demand for compute power in the AI industry.
Apple may collaborate with Nvidia to facilitate this re-entry into server manufacturing.

stories.title: Claude comes for Gemini with its own take on Docs and Slides
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Anthropic's Claude is launching integrated Docs and Slides tools, allowing users to create documents and presentations directly within the chat interface.
These new tools enable users to export, edit, and share the generated content from Claude.
Anthropic is also streamlining its user experience by merging regular chats and Cowork into a unified 'one Claude' interface.

stories.title: A brief history of AI executives calling for regulation
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: High-profile AI leaders (including Altman, Hassabis, Nadella) are publicly calling for AI regulation.
The consensus among these executives is that the industry needs to slow down to maintain control.
This signals a significant industry shift toward proactive governance concerns within the AI sector.

stories.title: Iran strikes on Amazon data centers caused permanent loss of customer data
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Iran's strikes resulted in permanent data loss at Amazon (AWS) data centers.
The physical damage surpassed the resilience capabilities designed into AWS services.
The incident highlights vulnerabilities of critical cloud infrastructure to geopolitical conflict.

stories.title: The Roman telescope has enough gas for 22 years, double NASA's expectations
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The Roman Space Telescope is pioneering in-space refueling capabilities.
Its fuel reserves are projected to last for 22 years, exceeding initial NASA estimates.
This marks a significant technological advancement for deep-space observatory longevity.

stories.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ScienceBuddy, an interactive workspace designed to integrate continually improving scientific AI agents into researcher workflows.
Features a core paradigm of 'recursive-in-recursive self-improvement,' combining harness evolution with model reinforcement learning.
The system learns continuously by transforming researcher requests, feedback, and execution evidence into new tasks and evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: PhysStream: Streaming Physics-Grounded Video Generation with Structured Scene Memory and Fine-Grained Motion Control
stories.author: Lingjie Liu
bullet_points: PhysStream is a new autoregressive model designed for physics-grounded image-to-video synthesis.
It addresses limitations in current controllable video generation by moving beyond coarse prompts to fine-grained, physically meaningful manipulation.
The model incorporates structured scene memory and aims to control dynamics based on physics rather than just pixel-space signals.

stories.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
stories.author: Ali Şenol
bullet_points: Introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only framework to improve LLM reliability.
CoSQ makes answer commitment conditional on an explicit assessment of the required factual information.
Evaluated across multiple model families on the TruthfulQA dataset to control for LLM hallucination/weak support.

stories.title: JustFit: 200K-Token LLM Serving on a 24 GiB Laptop with Just-in-Time State Management
stories.author: Yuhua Chen
bullet_points: Introduces JustFit, an MLX-based inference runtime designed to run large LLMs (200K tokens) on constrained hardware like a 24 GiB laptop.
Achieves memory efficiency through novel techniques: KVExec for compressed KV execution, PhaseSwap for component residency, and StateTrans for state-preserving transitions.
The system dynamically manages memory by coordinating just-in-time materialization and release, independent of model-weight quantization.

stories.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ScienceBuddy, an interactive workspace designed to integrate continually improving scientific AI agents into researcher workflows.
Features a core mechanism of 'recursive-in-recursive self-improvement,' combining harness evolution with model reinforcement learning.
The system learns continuously by transforming researcher requests, feedback, and execution evidence into new tasks and evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
stories.author: Ali Şenol
bullet_points: Introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only framework designed to improve LLM reliability.
CoSQ makes answer commitment conditional on an explicit assessment of the required factual support, addressing LLM hallucination.
Evaluated across multiple model families and conditions on the TruthfulQA benchmark to test selective risk control.

stories.title: Large Language Models Develop Belief State Geometry In-Context
stories.author: Xavier Poncini
bullet_points: The research investigates the internal representations within Large Language Models (LLMs) that enable In-Context Learning (ICL).
The study tests LLMs' ability to infer the 'belief state'—the posterior distribution over hidden states—when prompted with data generated from Hidden Markov Models (HMMs).
The findings suggest that LLMs may develop a form of 'Belief State Geometry' to support complex reasoning during ICL.

stories.title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
stories.author: polyphilz
bullet_points: A 4B parameter model was trained to optimize database query plans.
The model demonstrated a significant performance improvement, achieving 81% faster query plans than standard Postgres.
This represents a potential AI application in database performance tuning and optimization.

stories.title: Build real-time voice applications with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe
stories.author: thorwebdev
bullet_points: Google has released new Gemini Live models via the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.
These updates specifically enable the building of real-time voice applications.
The integration leverages Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe capabilities.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary models (Claude) and local, open-weight LLMs (via Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: The sexy AI-powered dating app scams are here
stories.author: Yael Grauer
bullet_points: A security researcher uncovered a fraudulent dating app named Dora.
The scam involved AI-powered tactics, exemplified by a simulated incoming call.
The story highlights the growing threat of sophisticated AI-driven scams in social/dating platforms.

stories.title: Lawmakers target Flock cameras with a threat to highway funding
stories.author: Paresh Dave, wired.com
bullet_points: Lawmakers are proposing legislation to restrict the use of Flock cameras.
The proposed bipartisan bill would limit Flock cameras to specific public safety applications.
The legislation is tied to potential threats or changes in highway funding.

stories.title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
stories.author: Ratul Mahajan
bullet_points: The paper addresses 'agentic societies,' defined as autonomous AI agent collectives coordinating across differing trust boundaries.
Experimental results indicate that current communication and control mechanisms ('harnesses') are insufficient for achieving satisfactory outcomes, even with honest agents.
The research highlights vulnerabilities where faulty or malicious agents can disrupt collaboration and pursue harmful objectives.

stories.title: LACE: Layer-Wise Compression for Dynamic Frame Rate Codecs
stories.author: Shinji Watanabe
bullet_points: The research addresses the high computational cost of neural audio codecs due to long sequence lengths from high frame rates.
LACE proposes using dynamic frame rate codecs to reduce effective frame rates by merging multiple frames.
The method improves upon prior work by applying compression across multiple quantization layers, unlike methods that use a single compression step.

stories.title: ENCP: Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction for Vision-and-Language Navigation
stories.author: Muhamad Risqi U. Saputra
bullet_points: The paper introduces ENCP, a method for Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction (CP) tailored for Vision-Language-Navigation (VLN) models.
Uncertainty estimation is highlighted as a critical need in VLN to ensure safer and more reliable navigation decisions.
The research addresses a limitation of standard CP in VLN, where sequential steps prevent standard calibration from guaranteeing coverage.

stories.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
stories.author: Amir Feder
bullet_points: Addresses the difficulty in evaluating LLM assistants' social reasoning due to subjective user narratives and lack of ground truth for social properties.
Introduces 'Fuse,' a multi-agent simulation framework specifically designed to study user-mediated social reasoning in LLMs.
Focuses on improving the reliability and verifiability of social advice provided by large language model assistants.

stories.title: Det-LIME: Detector-Aware, Multi-Instance Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations for Automated Marine Mammal Detection
stories.author: Brinnae Bent
bullet_points: Introduces Det-LIME, a new explainability technique designed for object detection tasks in marine mammal research.
Addresses a gap where existing explainability tools fail to account for multiple detections or colonial life histories in imagery.
Focuses on making black-box object detectors more transparent and usable within real-world conservation workflows.

stories.title: ENCP: Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction for Vision-and-Language Navigation
stories.author: Muhamad Risqi U. Saputra
bullet_points: The paper introduces ENCP, an Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction method for Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN).
Uncertainty estimation is crucial in VLN to ensure agents make safer and more reliable navigation decisions.
Standard Conformal Prediction fails in sequential VLN tasks, necessitating this novel, episode-normalized approach for coverage guarantees.

stories.title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
stories.author: David Simchi-Levi
bullet_points: Addresses the problem of transferring systematic bias from a large teacher LLM to a smaller student model during distillation.
Proposes 'Coupled Calibration and Learning' (CCL) to mitigate teacher bias, especially under covariate shift.
Offers a solution for LLM distillation scenarios where target-domain reward feedback is unavailable.

stories.title: Tables Decoded: DELTA for Structure, TARQA for Understanding
stories.author: Ganesh Ramakrishnan
bullet_points: The research addresses the core task of table understanding, specifically table reconstruction and TabVQA.
It proposes a novel approach using structured textual representations instead of relying solely on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) operating on table images.
This textual method is presented as more scalable and better suited for alignment with Large Language Models (LLMs) by removing the need for visual encoders.

stories.title: OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run
stories.author: Harry Grieve
bullet_points: Addresses the reproducibility crisis in open-source language model training.
Identifies non-associativity of floating-point arithmetic as a core barrier to verification.
Highlights the gap between framework-level determinism and cross-hardware reproducibility.

stories.title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity
stories.author: Usman Aleem
bullet_points: The research investigates how model pruning affects the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) specifically in context-grounded tool calling for smart home applications.
It systematically compares degradation across four different LLMs and various pruning techniques (depth, width, hybrid, MoE) spanning different architectures.
The study evaluates the impact of pruning on practical tasks using a large dataset (over 19,500 instances) after supervised fine-tuning (SFT).

stories.title: LACE: Layer-Wise Compression for Dynamic Frame Rate Codecs
stories.author: Shinji Watanabe
bullet_points: The research addresses the high computational cost of neural audio codecs used in speech language modeling due to long sequence lengths.
The proposed LACE method uses dynamic frame rate codecs to reduce effective frame rate by merging multiple frames.
LACE improves upon prior methods by applying compression across multiple quantization layers, unlike previous single-step approaches.

stories.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
stories.author: Amir Feder
bullet_points: Addresses the difficulty in evaluating the social reasoning capabilities of LLM assistants.
Proposes 'Fuse,' a multi-agent simulation framework designed to study user-mediated social reasoning.
Tackles the challenge of subjective user narratives and the lack of verifiable ground truth for social properties like intentions.

stories.title: Enhancing Accessibility of Medical Texts through Large Language Model-Driven Plain Language Adaptation
stories.author: Hsin-Hsi Chen
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate Plain Language Adaptation (PLA) for medical texts.
PLA aims to simplify complex healthcare jargon to improve patient reading comprehension and accessibility.
The work leverages LLMs (like GPT and BART) for PLA, particularly in scenarios with limited task-specific data (zero/few-shot learning).

stories.title: Mistral X Mozilla: Private, Multilingual AI Browsing
stories.author: vertigoruntime
bullet_points: Collaboration between Mistral AI and Mozilla on AI browsing technology.
The resulting product emphasizes privacy and multilingual capabilities.
Indicates a trend toward privacy-focused, advanced AI integration in web browsing.

stories.title: Firebase AI Logic in Angular: Client-Side Gemini Without a Custom Backend
stories.author: wayne_gakuo
bullet_points: Demonstrates using Firebase AI Logic to implement Gemini capabilities directly on the client side within an Angular application.
Highlights a significant architectural shift by removing the need for a custom backend for AI processing.
Provides a practical, developer-focused tutorial for integrating advanced AI features into web frontends.
